title: Types after the round trip
prompt: This program saves the 12 lesson trips twice, as CSV and as Parquet, and reads both back without a schema. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
trips.select("trip_id", "passenger_count", "fare").write.mode("overwrite").csv("/tmp/c1/csv", header=True)
trips.select("trip_id", "passenger_count", "fare").write.mode("overwrite").parquet("/tmp/c1/parquet")

from_csv = spark.read.csv("/tmp/c1/csv", header=True)
from_parquet = spark.read.parquet("/tmp/c1/parquet")
print(from_csv.dtypes)
print(from_parquet.dtypes)
print(from_csv.count(), from_parquet.count())
hints: `dtypes` is a list of `(name, type)` pairs, in column order.
A CSV file has no types: read without a schema or `inferSchema`, every column is text.
Parquet keeps the schema it was written with. Neither format adds or drops rows.
